title: に vs で (Location of Existence vs Location of Action)
distinction: Use に with static verbs of existence (あります, います, 住みます) to specify WHERE something exists. Use で with dynamic action verbs (勉強します, 食べます, 買います) to specify WHERE an action occurs, or the MEANS used.

comparisonExamples.explanation: あります is a verb of existence; static presence requires に.
読みます is an active verb; the location where the action occurs requires で.

title: は vs が (Topic vs Subject / Focus)
distinction: は marks the shared topic already known to speakers or establishes contrast. が identifies new information, specific subjects, or answers question words (だれが, なにが).

comparisonExamples.explanation: わたし establishes the topic of identity.
Question words like だれ cannot take は as topic; they take が.

title: に vs へ (Goal / Destination vs Direction of Motion)
distinction: に emphasizes the specific destination reached. へ (pronounced 'e') emphasizes the direction toward which motion is oriented.

comparisonExamples.explanation: Direction of travel takes へ (or destination に).

title: と vs で (Accompaniment vs Means / Solo)
distinction: と specifies doing something with another person (家族と). で specifies the means/method, or doing an action alone (一人で).

comparisonExamples.sentence: 友だち___映画を見ました。
comparisonExamples.explanation: Watching a movie together with a companion requires と.
Acting alone is a condition/mode of action, requiring で.
